pageTitle: Prepare to respond to a claim for possession of a rented property
serviceName: Respond to a claim for possession of a rented property
caption: Prepare to:
heading: Respond to a claim for possession of a rented property
pilotBanner: This guide is for the online possession service, which is only available in some courts.
intro: This step-by-step guide can help you prepare to respond to a claim for possession of a rented property.
sectionCount: Each section explains what you will be asked and any documents you may need. There are {{number}} sections. Some are optional and may not apply to you.
pilotScope: You can only respond online if the letter about your claim tells you to. If it does not, follow the instructions in the letter.
readyHeading: When you are ready to complete the form
readyText: Once you are ready to complete the form, you can
readyLink: respond to a property possession claim online
claimantCanSeeAnswers: The claimant will be able to see your answers.

content.text: We will ask you to confirm your:

items: name
address
date of birth
contact preferences

tenancy.title: Tenancy, occupation contract or licence agreement

content.text: When your landlord (the claimant) made their claim, they provided information about your agreement.
We will ask you to confirm:

items: your tenancy, occupation contract, or licence agreement and when it started
whether your landlord gave you notice before starting possession proceedings, and when you received it

payments.title: Payments or agreements since the claim was made

content.text: If the claim against you is based on rent arrears, we will ask you to confirm:

items: how much money you owe
whether you have paid any money since the claim was made – if you have, you will be asked how much you paid and when
whether you have made an agreement with your landlord to repay what you owe – if you have, you will be asked how much you agreed to pay, how often you will pay and when you made this agreement

content.text: If you have not made an agreement with your landlord, you can offer to pay what you owe in instalments. We will ask:

items: how much you could afford to pay in addition to your current rent
how often you can make this payment
any dependants you have (people you look after financially)
other adults that live in your home
whether you would have anywhere else to live if you were asked to leave your home
any personal circumstances that have led to your case that you think a judge should know about
any exceptional hardship you would experience if you were asked to leave your home

content.text: A judge can use details about your income and expenses to reach a decision on your case, and to decide how much you could afford to repay if you owe any money in rent payments.
If you choose to give any details, we will ask you about:

items: your regular income
any benefits you receive
if you have applied for Universal Credit
any priority debts
other regular expenses

content.text: We may also ask you to upload financial documents or other supporting evidence.

disputing.title: Disputing other parts of the claim

content.text: If any part of the claim against you is not about rent arrears, we will ask you to:

items: review the claim
tell us if you disagree with any part of it

content.text: You can dispute part of the claim if you think the claimant has provided incorrect information or you disagree with what they have said. For example, you may think they did not follow the correct legal procedure, or a document they uploaded is not valid.
A counterclaim is a separate claim that you can make alongside your response to the claim against you. In a counterclaim, you say that a party owes you something. This can be money or something else.

items: if you want to make a counterclaim
to pay a fee to make a counterclaim, unless you are eligible for help with fees

support.title: Tell us if you need support

content.text: Some people need support to use HMCTS services.
You can ask for support such as:

items: a language interpreter
reasonable adjustments if you have a health condition or disability
special measures to help you feel safe at court

content.text: To ask for an interpreter or special measures, contact the court dealing with your case.
You may also be able to choose to answer equality and diversity questions.
You will be able to review all your answers and make any changes before you submit your response.
